subject: VPC fabric convergence & handoff checklist
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@telcoco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: netbridge-ops@telcoco.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: VPC fabric convergence & handoff checklist

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We ran the topology review with our network team and have a few items to lock before we accept the handoff: 

- Verify control-plane peering (mTLS certs + rotation cadence) across the on-prem border routers.
- Confirm egress filtering behavior when the Redwood side fails over to the backup tunnel (we need deterministic SNAT ranges).
- A short runbook for badge-ops to escalate if KV-cache eviction patterns cause request spikes.
- Evidence of config drift checks (snapshots + diff cadence).

I attached our current topo (telcoco-vpc-topo.pdf) and a simple list of our operational constraints. Can you provide a handoff checklist and indicate which items Redwood will own vs Telcoco? We need this to get sign-off from our Security and Network teams by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lin
NetOps Manager, Telcoco

Attachment: telcoco-vpc-topo.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@telcoco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: VPC fabric convergence & handoff checklist

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a draft handoff checklist and called out owner (Redwood / Telcoco) and verification steps. Key notes up front:

- Control plane peering: Redwood will generate the mTLS cert bundle and provide rotation scripts. Telcoco to provide CA pinning fingerprint and test user for rotation validation.
- Egress failover: Redwood will document the SNAT ranges and provide a failover test plan; Telcoco must confirm permitted CIDR ranges on their firewall.
- KV-cache runbook: Redwood owns initial mitigation (automatic cache bumping and autoscaling hooks). Telcoco will monitor application-level latency and escalate per the runbook.
- Config drift: Redwood will deliver nightly snapshots and a weekly drift digest; Telcoco will subscribe to the digest and confirm any exceptions.

I'm attaching the checklist (redwood-vpc-handoff-checklist.xlsx) and a short egress test plan (egress-test-plan.md). The checklist includes: 
  * Acceptance criteria (control-plane stable for 24h)
  * Test steps (connectivity, cert rotation, KV fault injection, ingress/egress smoke tests)
  * Rollback conditions and ownership matrix

Proposed timeline:
- Tue: Redwood completes cert bundle + draft rotation script (we'll share a vault-access token for tests)
- Wed: Joint run of cert rotation and failover smoke tests (30–60m)
- Thu: KV-cache fault injection and load pass (2h window)
- Fri: Final sign-off, security checklist closure

Can Kimberly and Marissa verify the acceptance criteria and add any operational checks we should include (observability hooks, tracepoint coverage, alert thresholds)?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-vpc-handoff-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), egress-test-plan.md (text/markdown)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@telcoco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: VPC fabric convergence & handoff checklist

Adding a couple of practical checks from the ops side: 

- Observability: ensure tenant-level traces include control-plane hop IDs and KV cache hit/miss ratio tagged by tenant id. Alert if miss ratio > 8% for 10 min.
- Latency SLOs: define 95th percentile token-latency targets for the on-prem gateway; add smoke test in egress plan that measures P95 over a 5-minute sliding window during the load test.
- Secrets: rotation token lifetime should be <= 72h for test tokens; production KV rotation cadence will be weekly.
- Rollback: include a deterministic step to re-point the control-plane to the previous cert bundle and a one-click toggle in the management console (we'll provide the toggle UI change).

I updated the checklist with these rows and a short verification script snippet. Marissa — please add the customer-readiness confirmation steps (security attestations and contact list for escalation).

-kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@telcoco.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: VPC fabric convergence & handoff checklist

Sara — quick confirmation from our side: the updated checklist now includes a Security sign-off block (SOC2 scoping: access logs, key rotation evidence, MFA on admin console) and a contact matrix for escalations (on-call + manager). Proposed time for the joint smoke tests: Wed 09:30–10:30 CET — that works for our on-call rotation.

If that window is good for you, I'll record the test session and upload the artifacts to the Drive link in the checklist.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
